newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks fight off profit-taking to close higher.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks fight off profit-taking to close higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks fought off bouts of profit-taking, rallying to a strong close on Thursday led by continued strength in the banking sector, brokers said.

"The market is mixed. But good volume was maintained in the afternoon showing that buying sentiment and profit-taking are both strong forces at this level," said Sean Li, associate director of Amsteel Securities.

The Hang Seng Index fluctuated throughout the day in a 100-point range, closing up 40.62 points at 12,436.80. Turnover was a healthy HK$6.87 billion, although substantially down from Wednesday's HK$9.142 billion.
"There is a certain amount of nervousness at this level but few big sellers," said one broker with an international house.
The Hang Seng Index soared to a new all time high of 12,602.34 on Wednesday, then fell to end the day down 94.52 points at 12,396.18.

Many investors variously view the blue chip sector, and the market leaders, HSBC, Sun Hung Kai Properties and Henderson Land in particular, as too expensive, while others are still accumulating them, brokers said.

HSBC is still the market favourite, said Amsteel's Li. HSBC closed up HK$1.50 at HK$153.00 after matching its all time high of HK$153.50. The share has outperformed the market by about eight percent over the past 12 months.
The finance sector led the market, while utilities were the worst performing sector. Properties and the commercial and industrial sector finish the day up, after suffering bouts of profit-taking.
Hong Kong Telecom lost HK$0.20 to close at HK$13.60, while Hongkong Electric edged up HK$0.10 to HK$25.05.

In the property sector, Cheung Kong dropped HK$0.25 to HK$61.75 and New World fell HK$0.20 to HK$42.80. Brokers said many property counters were overvalued and they were waiting to see what kinds of properties the companies would bring to market in the next couple of months.

Sun Hung Kai & Co resumed trading on Thursday. The share fell HK$0.30 to HK$2.10. The company announced a two-for-five rights issue at HK$1.80 per rights share, aimed at raising HK$498 million to reduce debt and provide working capital.
Guangzhou Investment said it was offering 61.2 million new shares at a price of HK2.555 per share and listing the shares in Singapore. The share closed down HK$0.075 at HK$2.60.
